abstracts.abstract: The increasing complexity of service-oriented architectures in cloud-native environments demands fundamental rethinking of traditional service composition paradigms. Conventional approaches relying on static service binding and centralized orchestration mechanisms struggle to accommodate the dynamic nature of modern distributed systems. This paper introduces a novel paradigm for intent-driven service composition that shifts from imperative orchestration specifications to declarative intent declarations. We formalize a theoretical framework based on autonomic computing principles, wherein composition goals are expressed as high-level business objectives rather than low-level workflow specifications. The framework decomposes service composition into three interconnected phases: intent specification, adaptive service discovery, and context-aware binding. We establish theoretical foundations proving that this paradigm achieves superior adaptability under volatile conditions compared to traditional choreography models. Through rigorous mathematical modeling using stochastic processes, we demonstrate that intent-driven composition exhibits convergence properties within bounded adaptation time. The analysis reveals that our approach reduces composition overhead by logarithmic factors while maintaining SLA compliance across heterogeneous service ecosystems. This work represents a fundamental paradigm shift from process-centric to outcome-centric service orchestration, opening new research directions in adaptive service management for next-generation computing platforms.

Service-level agreements in multi-cloud service compositions face significant challenges due to the inherent uncertainty in provider performance and runtime variability. Existing SLA models predominantly rely on static guarantees that inadequately capture the probabilistic nature of cloud service behavior. This paper presents an enhanced probabilistic SLA framework that explicitly models and manages performance uncertainty through novel stochastic contract mechanisms. The proposed framework introduces distribution-aware SLA clauses that characterize provider reliability using historical performance data combined with predictive analytics. We develop a formal verification methodology for reasoning about SLA satisfaction across interdependent services in composition scenarios. The approach utilizes probabilistic model checking to assess violation risks under various runtime conditions. Theoretical analysis establishes that our framework achieves a 40% reduction in expected SLA violations compared to conventional static models by incorporating accurate uncertainty quantification. Furthermore, we prove that the overhead of probabilistic verification remains tractable through abstraction techniques that preserve essential stochastic properties. The work significantly advances service quality management by providing formal foundations for handling uncertainty in service agreements, representing a substantial improvement over existing approaches that treat SLA compliance as a deterministic problem.

The proliferation of microservices architectures has introduced unprecedented challenges in service management, demanding fundamentally new approaches to distributed monitoring and adaptive scaling. This paper presents IntelliMesh, a next-generation microservices management platform that embodies a paradigm shift toward intent-based and self-healing service orchestration. The system architecture comprises three interconnected components: an intent translation layer that converts high-level business objectives into executable service configurations, a distributed observability engine leveraging extended Berkeley Packet Filter technology for fine-grained telemetry with minimal performance overhead, and a reinforcement learning-driven autoscaler that continuously optimizes resource allocation based on multi-objective cost-performance tradeoffs. The autoscaler employs deep Q-networks trained on workload patterns specific to service-oriented applications, achieving adaptive scaling decisions that reduce operational costs while maintaining quality guarantees. We detail the implementation of the self-healing mechanisms that automatically detect and recover from service failures through proactive health checking and intelligent request routing. The platform was evaluated through deployment in a production e-commerce environment managing over 10,000 microservices across multiple availability zones. Results demonstrate that the intent-driven orchestration model reduces configuration complexity by 60% while the ML-based autoscaling achieves 35% cost reduction compared to rule-based approaches. This work establishes a new architectural pattern for service management in cloud-native environments.

Testing microservice-based applications remains a significant challenge due to complex service interactions, asynchronous communication patterns, and intricate state dependencies across distributed components. Current testing approaches suffer from inadequate coverage of service compositions and unreliable results stemming from simplistic mocking strategies. This paper presents TestFlow, an improved testing framework specifically designed for microservice environments that addresses these critical limitations. The framework introduces three key innovations: contract-based test generation that automatically extracts interface specifications from service APIs and produces comprehensive test suites, stateful mocking mechanisms that replicate realistic service behaviors and inter-service dependencies, and adaptive test prioritization using historical failure patterns combined with code change impact analysis. The system architecture incorporates a plugin-based design enabling seamless integration with continuous integration and deployment pipelines supporting major container orchestration platforms. We implemented TestFlow as an open-source toolkit and evaluated its effectiveness across twelve production microservice systems spanning various application domains. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves 78% improvement in fault detection rate compared to traditional testing methods while reducing test execution time by 60% through intelligent test parallelization. TestFlow represents a significant advancement in service testing capabilities, providing development teams with practical tools that can be adopted with minimal changes to existing development processes.
